tuning.starter:
reading = float(input('Frequency (Hz): '))
# Report whether the reading is within 1 Hz of A4.

cases.name: Typed 440.5
cases.expected: Frequency (Hz): 440.5 Hz is in tune with A4.

cases.name: Typed 445
cases.expected: Frequency (Hz): 445.0 Hz is 5.0 Hz away from A4.

cases.name: Typed 441
cases.expected: Frequency (Hz): 441.0 Hz is in tune with A4.

cases.name: Typed 438.9
cases.expected: Frequency (Hz): 438.9 Hz is 1.1 Hz away from A4.

cases.name: Typed 439
cases.expected: Frequency (Hz): 439.0 Hz is in tune with A4.

tuning.check:
import re
assert not re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "elif is not part of this lecture yet."
assert not re.search(r"\b(and|or|not)\b", __code__), "and, or and not are not part of this lecture yet; use separate if statements."
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1 and re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "Use exactly one if with an else."
assert "abs(" in __code__, "Use abs() so that a reading below 440 and a reading above 440 are handled by the same comparison."
assert "<=" in __code__ or ">" in __code__, "A difference of exactly 1 Hz counts as in tune; check the boundary."
assert len(__stdout__.strip().splitlines()) == 1, "Print one line."
hints: `abs(reading - 440)` is the distance from A4 whether the reading is sharp or flat. Compare that one number with 1.
tuning.answerNote: abs() folds the two sides of 440 into one distance, so one comparison covers sharp and flat readings. The boundary 441 is in tune because the test is <=.

equilateral.starter:
a = float(input('Side a: '))
b = float(input('Side b: '))
c = float(input('Side c: '))
# Report whether the triangle is equilateral.

cases.name: Typed 3 3 3
cases.expected: Side a: Side b: Side c: A triangle with sides 3.0, 3.0 and 3.0 is equilateral.

cases.name: Typed 3 4 3
cases.expected: Side a: Side b: Side c: A triangle with sides 3.0, 4.0 and 3.0 is not equilateral.

cases.name: Typed 2.5 2.5 2.5
cases.expected: Side a: Side b: Side c: A triangle with sides 2.5, 2.5 and 2.5 is equilateral.

cases.name: Typed 5 5 5.5
cases.expected: Side a: Side b: Side c: A triangle with sides 5.0, 5.0 and 5.5 is not equilateral.

cases.name: Typed 6 7 8
cases.expected: Side a: Side b: Side c: A triangle with sides 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 is not equilateral.

equilateral.check:
import re
assert not re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "elif is not part of this lecture yet."
assert not re.search(r"\b(and|or|not)\b", __code__), "and, or and not are not part of this lecture yet; use separate if statements."
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) >= 2, "Compare the sides with separate if statements, one pair per if."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "Start with kind = 'equilateral' and let the if statements change it; no else is needed."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Print once, after the if statements."
assert "==" in __code__ or "!=" in __code__, "Compare the sides with == or !=."
hints: Store `kind = 'equilateral'` first. Then an `if` that compares `a` with `b` and another that compares `b` with `c` can each change it to `'not equilateral'`. If `a` equals `b` and `b` equals `c`, then `a` equals `c` as well, so two comparisons are enough.
equilateral.answerNote: Two comparisons cover all three pairs: when a == b and b == c, a == c follows. Each if overrides the default on its own, so no and is needed.

phone.starter:
minutes = int(input('Minutes: '))
texts = int(input('Texts: '))
# Print the bill, one charge per line.

cases.name: Typed 60 and 70
cases.expected:
Minutes: Texts: Base plan: $15.00
Extra minutes: $2.50
Extra texts: $3.00
911 fee: $0.44
Tax: $3.14
Total: $24.08

cases.name: Typed 50 and 50
cases.expected:
Minutes: Texts: Base plan: $15.00
911 fee: $0.44
Tax: $2.32
Total: $17.76

cases.name: Typed 120 and 10
cases.expected:
Minutes: Texts: Base plan: $15.00
Extra minutes: $17.50
911 fee: $0.44
Tax: $4.94
Total: $37.88

cases.name: Typed 0 and 51
cases.expected:
Minutes: Texts: Base plan: $15.00
Extra texts: $0.15
911 fee: $0.44
Tax: $2.34
Total: $17.93

cases.name: Typed 51 and 51
cases.expected:
Minutes: Texts: Base plan: $15.00
Extra minutes: $0.25
Extra texts: $0.15
911 fee: $0.44
Tax: $2.38
Total: $18.22

phone.check:
import re
assert not re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "elif is not part of this lecture yet."
assert not re.search(r"\b(and|or|not)\b", __code__), "and, or and not are not part of this lecture yet; use separate if statements."
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 2, "Use two separate if statements: one for the extra minutes and one for the extra texts."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "No else is needed: when there is no extra charge, nothing is printed for it."
assert re.search(r":[^}]*\.2f\}", __source__), "Show every amount with two decimal places."
lines = __stdout__.strip().splitlines()
assert 4 <= len(lines) <= 6, "Print the base plan, any extra charges, the 911 fee, the tax and the total, one per line."
assert "Base plan:" in lines[0] and lines[-1].startswith("Total:"), "Start with the base plan and end with the total."
hints: Keep a running `subtotal` that starts at 15.00 + 0.44. Each `if` adds its extra charge to it and prints its own line. The tax is 15 percent of the subtotal, and the total is the subtotal plus the tax.
The extra minutes cost `(minutes - 50) * 0.25`, but only when `minutes > 50`. A plan with exactly 50 minutes has no extra charge, so 50 must not print a line.
`${extra_minutes:.2f}` prints the amount with two decimals. Only print an extra line when there is an extra charge, so put the print inside the if.
phone.answerNote: Each if adds its charge to the subtotal and prints its own line, so the tax and total come out right whether zero, one or both extras apply.
